column1: # Retrospective bench points — every tagged GitHub artifact (rakupp-macos-universal,
# arm64 slice) re-run on ONE machine in ONE sitting: 2026-08-31, Darwin 24.6,
# Apple M3, macOS 15.7.4. Supersedes the 2026-08-21 Darwin 25.5 sitting entirely,
# which covered `hashfill` only and whose Raku++ binaries ran 1.3-1.5x slow.
# Each release is measured against the Rakudo that was CURRENT ON ITS RELEASE
# built from source, native arm64, one toolchain for all three. NOTE MoarVM has
# no JIT backend on arm64 (it compiles src/jit/stub.o), so this rakudo column is
# NOT comparable with one measured on an x86_64 host, which does have the JIT.
# Method: tools/run-bench.raku, 7 runs per kernel, first discarded, minimum of
# the remaining 6, lanes interleaved, output correctness-gated before timing —
# every engine agreed on every row. Because the rakudo lane is re-measured once
# per release rather than once per sitting, its within-era spread is a direct
# noise figure: ~2%, except `sortby`, which is bimodal at ~168/198ms and should
# gen-dashboard merges these as an OVERRIDE per engine, not gap-fill: a tag's
# own committed tables were measured on whatever machine that release had, and
# their rakudo column ran under Rosetta 2 until 2026-08-31. Engines absent here
# RAKUDO IS NOT IN THIS FILE. Rakudo ships monthly, so it is a constant between
# its own releases and belongs to a DATE, not to a Raku++ tag; measuring it per
# tag drew noise as signal (19% on sortby). It lives in rakudo-eras.tsv and is
# assigned by date to every point, tagged or not.
# Not covered: v0.1.0, v0.5.0 and v1.1.5 ship no release binary, so they have no
# measured point and the charts draw a gap. `arraypush` is absent before v1.5.2:
# Array.push was quadratic and a single run exceeds 10s, so it is omitted rather
# than estimated. Reproduce with tools/rakupp-bench-sweep.sh in the rakupp repo.
# v3.25.0 measured 2026-09-03 in its own sitting, same method and machine
# (Darwin 24.6, Apple M3): the released rakupp-macos-universal.tar.gz, sha256
# verified against its published .sha256, arm64 slice (the binary reports
# arm64-darwin at run time), rakudo 2026.08 from source. Note the CI artifact is
# built with clang 21 where the local build uses clang 17.
# 2026-09-01, same machine: v3.24.0's artifact added in a SECOND sitting.
# Same method and same Rakudo era as the 2026-08-31 rows above; the rakudo
# lane re-measured within 1.5% of them, which is inside the ~2% noise this
# file documents, so the two sittings are comparable. Added because
# v3.24.0's own committed BENCHMARKS.md predates the eight-carry-chain
# bigint work (49bdf34) and reported bigint ~10x slow.
